starting_principles: Euclidean angle-sum theorem for a planar triangle: sum of interior angles is $180^\circ$
Cyclic quadrilateral property: sum of opposite interior angles is $180^\circ$
Definition of angular deviation $\delta$ as the net change in direction between incident ray and emergent ray
assumptions: Prism has a triangular cross-section with refracting apex angle $A$ between polished planar faces $AB$ and $AC$
Optical ray propagates strictly in the principal cross-sectional plane perpendicular to the refracting edge
Ray undergoes refraction at face $AB$ (angle of incidence $i$, angle of refraction $r_1$) and at face $AC$ (internal angle of incidence $r_2$, emergent angle $e$)

ordered_steps.description: Analyze the geometry of quadrilateral formed by prism apex $A$, refraction points $Q$ and $R$, and the intersection of normals $N$.
ordered_steps.operation: Sum opposite right angles to show quadrilateral $AQNR$ is cyclic: $\angle A + \angle QNR = 180^\circ$
assumptions_applied: Normals are perpendicular to the respective prism faces

ordered_steps.description: Apply the triangle angle-sum theorem to $\triangle QNR$ to relate the apex angle $A$ to internal refraction angles $r_1$ and $r_2$.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $\angle QNR = 180^\circ - A$ into the triangle sum equation
ordered_steps.result_equation: r_1 + r_2 + (180^\circ - A) = 180^\circ \implies A = r_1 + r_2

ordered_steps.description: Calculate the angular deviation $\delta_1$ suffered by the ray upon refraction at the first face $AB$.
ordered_steps.operation: Subtract $r_1$ from the angle of incidence $i$
assumptions_applied: Linear ray deviation toward normal at first refracting face

ordered_steps.description: Calculate the angular deviation $\delta_2$ suffered by the ray upon refraction and emergence at the second face $AC$.
ordered_steps.operation: Subtract internal incidence angle $r_2$ from the emergence angle $e$
assumptions_applied: Linear ray deviation away from normal at second refracting face

ordered_steps.description: Sum the deviations at both faces to compute the net deviation $\delta$ of the ray.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $\delta_1 = i - r_1$ and $\delta_2 = e - r_2$
assumptions_applied: Both individual deviations bend the ray in the same rotational sense (toward prism base)

ordered_steps.description: Substitute the apex angle relation $A = r_1 + r_2$ into the total deviation expression.

applicability_conditions: Valid for triangular prisms with flat planar faces with rays confined to the principal cross-sectional plane
Ray successfully transmits across both faces without undergoing total internal reflection at face $AC$
